description:
FILED s488a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by task #1834's CHECK 2 on op/inc.t, which
became COMPLETE at e2536f81 and whose 26 failing rows split into three classes;
this is the class of 8.

A `my` DECLARATION WITH AN INITIALIZER that carries a statement-modifier
`for`/`foreach` is a #138 DROP.  The announcement is LOUD (and inside a string
eval it DIES, per the s408 ruling), so nothing is silently wrong -- but the
statement is a compiler gap, not a refusal, and perl runs it.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL HEAD 46fb7645) -- the DISCRIMINATOR is the
declaration, not the modifier and not the operand:
    my @a = (1,2);
    $y  = ++$_ for @a;        # PCL: works, a = 2 3   (= perl)
    my $z; $z = ++$_ for @a;  # PCL: works, a = 3 4   (= perl)
    my $y = ++$_ for @a;      # PCL: DROPPED
      PCL: statement dropped at F line N: my $y = ++$_ for @a --
           Bug. Fell through. Missing case:
           [bless({'id'=>4,'type'=>'prefix_op'},'PPIreference'),
            bless({'id'=>0,'type'=>'funcall'},'PPIreference')]
      perl: runs it; @a becomes (2,3)
The operand does not matter (`for @a`, `for (5,6)`, `for *GLOB` all drop) and
neither does the expression (`my $y = $_ for *G` drops too, with
`['Token::Magic<$_>', funcall]`), so the missing case is the DECLARATION
statement's lowering meeting a statement modifier -- the `funcall` in the
message is the modifier's list.

WHERE IT COSTS ROWS: t/op/inc.t:381-389 is
    *GLOB126637 = [];
    eval 'my $y = ++$_ for *GLOB126637';
    like $@, qr/Modification of a read-only value/, '++*GLOB126637';
in eight spellings (++/--, pre/post, with and without `use integer`).  perl
dies "Modification of a read-only value attempted"; PCL dies with the drop
announcement, so `$@` does not match and all eight rows fail.  They are
attributed here in baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv's op/inc.t row.

NOTE on the other two classes of that file, for the record: 14 rows are
`... under use warnings 'imprecision'` (NS:Warnings-gated diagnostics are
absent -- `use warnings` is not modelled; owner #221) and 4 are `9466 case N`,
which need a `bless`ed object to be finalized at the end of a block
(NS:`DESTROY` called by garbage collector).
subject: a `my` declaration WITH an initializer plus a statement-modifier `for` is a #138 drop (`my $y = ++$_ for @a`) -- the same statement works without the `my`, and it costs t/op/inc.t 8 rows
